Measures
In this BFI data set, the 5 factors refer to the 5 composites included in the Big Five Inventory. Openness, which indicates one’s open-mindedness, creativity, and likelihood to embrace new experiences (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.6). Conscientiousness, which refers to one’s tendency to be reliable, organized, and disciplined (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.72). Extraversion, which refers to one’s social interactions and emotional expression (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.76). Agreeableness, which refers to one’s tendency to cooperate or desire to compete (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.7). and Neuroticism which refers to one’s tendency toward depression, anxiety, or negative feelings (Cronbach’s alpha =0.81).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for variables O2, C4, E1, E2, and A1 were reverse keyed.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text: This assignment analyzes the Attachment and Social Anxiety dataset by Jacob Lincoln, Liesbeth Tip, and Sofia De La Fuente Garcia, focusing on attachment-related anxiety, social interaction anxiety, and self-esteem.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text: This assignment analyzes the Attachment and Social Anxiety dataset by Jacob Lincoln, Liesbeth Tip, and Sofia De La Fuente Garcia, focusing on attachment-related anxiety, social interaction anxiety, and self-esteem.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text:
Methods
Participants were recruited via the University of Edinburgh’s online learning portal and social media platforms, as well as through word-of-mouth. A flyer with a link to the study was shared on these platforms along with a standard message explaining the purpose of the study, the inclusion criteria (i.e., must be over the age of 18), and the contact details of one of the researchers.
The participants followed a link to the questionnaire, which was created using the Online Surveys platform. Participants responded to 3 questionnaires to measure 1) Attachment-related anxiety, 2) Social anxiety and 3) Self-esteem. They were also asked to report their gender, age group, relationship status and ethnicity.

Participants
There were 63 participants in the study. Table 1 presents the demographic information of the participants.

Measures
There are three scales used in this analysis:

Experiences in Close Relationships Scale (shortened Attachment-Related Anxiety subscale). This subscale was shortened by only including the nine items that loaded most strongly on the Anxiety subscale in a factor analysis conducted by Sibley, Fischer & Liu (2005). This scale had a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.94.
Social Interaction Anxiety Scale, with a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.9.
Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, which had a Cronbach’s alpha of 0.85.

title: 9041 Assignment 2
text:
Data Analysis Strategy
Items were reverse-keyed in the scoring keys before calculating the scale scores. Items 5, 9, and 11 were reverse-keyed for Social Interaction Anxiety, while Items 2, 5, 6, 8, and 9 were reverse-keyed for Self-Esteem. No items were reverse-keyed for Attachment-Related Anxiety. Reverse-keyed items were indicated with a minus sign (-) in the scoring keys and were handled by scoreItems().

The table presents the mean, median, standard deviation, range, and Cronbach’s alpha for each scale. The mean score for Attachment-Related Anxiety was 3.4.
